Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1259 AM CDT Mon Aug 10 2026

Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE OHIO VALLEY AND CENTRAL APPALACHIANS...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts will be possible on
Tuesday from parts of the Ohio Valley into the central Appalachians
in the afternoon and evening. Isolated severe wind gusts and hail
will also be possible from parts of the central and northern Plains
into the Midwest.

...Ohio Valley/Central Appalachians...
At mid-levels, west-northwesterly flow will remain in place on
Tuesday from the northern Plains to the central Appalachians. At the
surface, a quasi-stationary front is forecast to be located from
northern Illinois east-southeastward into far northern Kentucky. To
the south of the front, surface dewpoints in the lower to mid 70s F
will result in moderate to strong instability by midday. Low-level
convergence along the boundary will likely be the focus for
convective initiation during the day. It appears that an intense
line segment could develop and move east-southeastward along and
near the frontal zone from mid afternoon to mid evening. However,
there is some uncertainty concerning where the boundary from morning
convection will be in the afternoon.

Forecast soundings along and to the south of the front from
east-central Illinois into far northern Kentucky at 21Z have MLCAPE
in the 2000 to 3500 J/kg range. Wind profiles along this
west-northwest to east-southeast corridor have directional shear in
the boundary layer with 40 to 50 knots of west-northwesterly flow in
the mid-levels. Some of this zone could have 0-6 km shear in the 40
to 50 knot range along with 0-3 km storm-relative helicity around
200 m2/s2. This would support supercells with severe wind gusts and
an isolated tornado threat. Some model forecasts, including the HRRR
suggest that an organized cold pool will develop during the late
afternoon. This scenario could result in a swath of wind damage
across parts of the Ohio Valley.

...Central and Northern Plains/Midwest...
At mid-levels, rising heights and west-northwesterly flow will be in
place over the north-central U.S. on Tuesday. At the surface, a cold
front will move southeastward across the northern High Plains, as a
low deepens across South Dakota. Ahead of the front, surface
dewpoints in the 60s and 70s F will contribute to moderate to strong
instability by afternoon. Low-level convergence will aid convective
initiation during the mid to late afternoon, with isolated storms
moving east-southeastward from the northern Plains into the Midwest.

Across the moist airmass, MLCAPE is forecast to peak in the 2000 to
3000 J/kg range with 0-6 km shear in the 35 to 45 knot range. This
will support supercells with isolated severe wind gusts and hail.
However, the rising mid-level heights and lack of large-scale ascent
could result in a more localized severe threat.

..Broyles.. 08/10/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0230 AM CDT Mon Aug 10 2026

Valid 121200Z - 131200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE CENTRAL AND NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts and hail will be possible
Wednesday afternoon and evening across parts of the central and
northern High Plains. Isolated severe wind gusts will also be
possible from parts of the mid Missouri Valley east-southeastward
into the southern Appalachians.

...Central and Northern Plains...
West-northwesterly mid-level flow will be in place on Wednesday from
the northern Plains into the Great Lakes. Within the flow, a subtle
shortwave trough is forecast to move into the central and northern
High plains during the afternoon. At the surface, a cold front is
forecast to move southward in the central Plains, with a lee trough
located in the High Plains. During the day, upslope flow will help
low-level convergence to become maximized along the lee trough,
which will the primary focus for convective initiation Wednesday
afternoon. Thunderstorms are expected to form near the trough and
move eastward across the central and northern High Plains during the
late afternoon and early evening.

Along the western edge of the moist airmass, surface dewpoints are
forecast to be mostly in the 60s F, which should result in moderate
instability by afternoon. Late afternoon forecast soundings from
North Platte, Nebraska northward to east of Rapid City, South Dakota
have 0-6 km shear in the 35 to 45 knot range with low to mid-level
lapse rates near 8 C/km. This will support a supercell threat during
the late afternoon and early evening. Supercells will be capable of
severe wind gusts and isolated large hail.

...Mid Missouri and Mid Mississippi Valley/Ohio Valley/Southern
Appalachians...
Mid-level northwesterly flow will be in place on Wednesday from the
Mid Missouri Valley into the Ohio Valley. At the surface, a very
moist airmass will also be in place over this same area. Surface
dewpoints in the 70s F will contribute to moderate to strong
instability by afternoon. Isolated to scattered thunderstorms will
be possible near outflow boundaries as low-level convergence becomes
maximized in the afternoon. Across much of this moist and unstable
airmass, moderate deep-layer shear will be in place supporting an
isolated wind-damage threat. The wind-damage threat should be
greatest in the late afternoon and early evening as low-level lapse
rates become steep.

..Broyles.. 08/10/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0354 AM CDT Mon Aug 10 2026

Valid 131200Z - 181200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Thursday/Day 4 to Saturday/Day 6...
A mid-level ridge is forecast to move eastward through the
north-central U.S. on Thursday and into the Great Lakes region on
Friday. At the surface, a moist axis is forecast to remain in place
from the central Plains east-southeastward into the lower Ohio
Valley. Moderate to strong instability along the moist axis will
make isolated severe thunderstorms possible each afternoon and
evening. Additionally, a severe threat may develop near mid-level
shortwave troughs that are forecast to move through the northern
Plains and Mid-Atlantic on Friday.

On Saturday, a mid-level shortwave trough is forecast to move
through the Great Lakes region. Moderate to strong instability may
be in place over much of Illinois, Indiana and Ohio by afternoon.
Along the northern edge of the stronger instability, isolated severe
thunderstorms will be possible from Lower Michigan eastward into the
central Appalachians Saturday afternoon. Additional severe storms
may develop along an axis of moderate instability over parts of the
central Plains in the afternoon and evening.

Concerning the severe potential from Thursday to Saturday,
considerable variance exists among the model solutions concerning
the position of features, suggesting uncertainty is still too great
to add a threat area.

...Sunday/Day 7 and Monday/Day 8...
From Sunday into Monday, a broad cyclonic flow pattern is forecast
to develop over the northeastern U.S. A cold front is forecast to
move southward across the central and southern Appalachians. This
boundary would be the primary focus for convective development each
afternoon and evening. Ahead of the front, surface dewpoints in the
70s F along with moderate to strong instability would likely support
an isolated severe threat. However, considerable uncertainty exists
concerning the timing of the front. For this reason, predictability
is low at this extended range.

..Broyles.. 08/10/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0747 AM CDT Mon Aug 10 2026

Valid 101300Z - 111200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE SOUTHERN
GREAT LAKES INTO THE MID-ATLANTIC STATES...PORTIONS OF THE UPPER
MIDWEST AND CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS...AND SOUTHERN ARIZONA...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts will be possible this afternoon
and evening from northern Illinois eastward into Pennsylvania.
Severe gusts and hail will also be possible from parts of the
central and northern Plains into the Midwest, with scattered severe
storms over southern Arizona.

...Synopsis...
Another highly uncertain and complex forecast with mesoscale
convective dependencies apparent this forecast update.  Water-vapor
imagery implies a belt of west-northwest mid to high-level flow
extending across the northern High Plains east through much of the
Midwest, and to the north of a flattened mid-level ridge extending
from the Four Corners to FL.  Embedded within the flow, a
convectively augmented disturbance over the southern Great Lakes
will move east into PA by early this afternoon. Another minor
perturbation over southwest MT this morning will quickly move into
the Dakotas by early evening and probably influence the severe
threat from SD into adjacent parts of IA/MN overnight.  

...IL to the Mid-Atlantic...
Radar mosaic this morning shows an organized line segment moving
east along the OH-Lake Erie shoreline and a couple of other
thunderstorm clusters over western OH and south-central PA.  The
Detroit, MI WSR-88D VAD showed a mid-level speed max associated with
the convectively augmented vorticity max moving east across the Lake
Erie vicinity.  Gradual intensification of storms is expected this
morning as the boundary layer heats downstream across OH into PA and
the Mid-Atlantic states (refer to MCD 1892 for short-term details
regarding the northeast OH thunderstorms).  Of particular note, the
12 UTC Pittsburgh, PA and Wilmington, OH raobs showed a moderate to
very unstable airmass (1800-2700 J/kg MLCAPE, respectively) in place
over the upper OH Valley.  Severe gusts capable of scattered wind
damage will be possible through the afternoon with any stronger
thunderstorms and clusters of storms.  Farther west, models show
storm redevelopment perhaps centered over northern IN/IL later this
afternoon/evening.  Shear/buoyancy profiles will support organized
storms, including supercells and linear clusters.  Damaging wind and
hail will be the primary hazards, though a tornado or two also could
occur.

...Dakotas into MN/IA...
Similar to previous forecast thinking, southeasterly low-level flow
will aid in the transport of seasonably rich moisture (mainly 60s F
surface dewpoints) north and west into SD.  Model forecast soundings
show large buoyancy developing by mid afternoon within the
aforementioned moist plume.  The weak impulse implied by model
guidance moving into western SD may enable at least isolated to
potentially scattered storms developing towards early evening over
western and central SD.  The 00z ECMWF and 00z HREF consensus
suggest a linear cluster evolves during the evening and grows
upscale into an MCS during the overnight moving east-southeast along
a residual frontal zone.  Have included an intensity level-1 to
denote this conditional but significant wind risk if this forecast
scenario occurs.  

...AZ...
Mid/upper easterly flow will persist today amid plentiful moisture
and strong heating.  This will support thunderstorm development once
again across higher terrain.  Scattered storms are forecast to
eventually develop with their cold pools coalescing over the lower
desert.  Based on the latest CAM guidance and inverted-V profiles
with marginally supportive shear for loose storm organization, have
upgraded a part of the lower desert into higher severe-wind
probabilities.  Widely scattered to scattered severe gusts 60-75 mph
are possible with this activity.  

...NE/CO/KS...
Scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop near a surface
trough across western NE/northeast CO by late afternoon/early
evening.  As the high-based storms mature into possibly a small
linear cluster and move into richer moisture with east extent, steep
low- to mid-level lapse rates will support severe gusts (60-75 mph)
and perhaps hail with this activity.

..Smith/Kerr.. 08/10/2026
